name: opencommerce
instructions:
# opencommerce design system: instructions for agents

Use this system to build opencommerce pages and interfaces from the user's brief. These instructions work with any agent that can read text and edit project files. The CLI is a local Node.js tool; no model account or agent-specific integration is needed for setup, discovery, installation or token checks.

## Start here

1. Read the project instructions and package.json. Identify the framework, package manager, stylesheet and import aliases. Use the user's requirements to decide whether to build new UI or restyle existing UI.
2. Read this guide, then the relevant component references. The library is at https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/components. Plain text is at https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/llms.txt; a complete copy is at https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/llms-full.txt.
3. Run `npx opencommerce-ds manifest --json` (or `describe --json`) before inventing anything. It lists every command, token, font, logo, template, size, component and rule. Unknown names are errors.
4. Reuse the library's components and variants. Do not recreate them from screenshots or guess their props. `npx opencommerce-ds component inspect <name> --json` returns the props and states that exist. `npx opencommerce-ds component emit` returns example code or JSX for values you checked.

## Install and prepare a project

Requires Node.js 20 or later. Run commands from the consuming project root, not the design-system repository.

```sh
npm install --save-dev github:anwarlemu/opencommerce-brand-cli#release
npx opencommerce-ds init
```

`npm install` installs the CLI only. `init` installs styles, fonts and agent instructions without converting existing components or creating conversion review tasks. It preserves other instructions already in the project. Inspect its warnings about a missing stylesheet or alias.

React components require React 19 or later, Tailwind CSS 4 and a working build. The installer follows components.json and TypeScript or JavaScript aliases; without aliases, it uses relative imports. Set up that framework first. Other frameworks can use the CSS tokens and styling guidance, but cannot render the React components.

For an existing interface that the user wants restyled, preview the explicit apply command:

```sh
npx -y github:anwarlemu/opencommerce-brand-cli#release apply --dry-run
npx -y github:anwarlemu/opencommerce-brand-cli#release apply
```

The apply command can adapt matching components, convert style values, and install agent rules and hooks. Color conversion is scoped to recognized components; unrelated palettes and artwork remain unchanged. The legacy bare command also converts styles; use explicit commands for setup and discovery. Subsequent runs resume review tasks. `--redo` repeats conversion. Review the diff and test existing behavior after conversion; a successful exit is not proof that the visual review is complete.

## Find, inspect and add components

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds list --json
npx opencommerce-ds show select
npx opencommerce-ds show select --json
npx opencommerce-ds add field select button --dry-run --json
npx opencommerce-ds add field select button --json
```

The add command above is an example, not the list required for every page. Choose items from `list`. `show` is read-only and works offline using the registry bundled with the CLI. `show --json` returns source, examples, usage rules, exports, dependencies and links. Hooks and helper libraries are included in the JSON index.

`add` copies source files and their transitive dependencies, installs missing npm packages, and wires the theme. Existing files are kept. Use `--overwrite` only when intentionally replacing local component changes. Read the returned file list and warnings. Generated imports and target files follow components.json and the project alias configuration. Existing utility files are preserved; brand helpers use their own names.

For HTTP-only agents, fetch `https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/r/index.json`, then `https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/r/<name>.json` or `https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/r/<name>.md`. Follow `requires` recursively. Each `files[].path` is relative to the source root; `files[].content` is the exact source. Each example lists its own `requires` and `packages`; install these too when using that example. Do not copy the example file as the component implementation. The CLI handles dependency ordering and theme installation for you.

The component reference states its source. `https://opencommerce-ds.vercel.app/r/audit.json` records the reference basis for all components. Some controls extend the site's patterns because the opencommerce site has no standalone equivalent (a select, a dialog, a toast); they use its fields, windows and keys. Do not describe extensions as exact copies of live controls.

## Compose the interface

- Follow the user's brief. For new pages, add the required content and behavior. When only restyling an existing page, preserve its content, links, order and behavior unless the user requests changes.
- Use component props and variants shown in the source. Read the named example functions before composing compound components. Keep client state inside a client component when using Next.js; imports of client components can still be rendered by server pages.
- Use design tokens for custom styles. `npx opencommerce-ds tokens <term> --json` finds values; `npx opencommerce-ds look <element-or-file> --json` explains styling by role. Use `var(--ds-*)` in CSS or the matching Tailwind utilities.
- Body text, buttons and links use Inter; headings use the display font stack; code, window bars and tags use the platform monospace. Keep one white page; use the provided flat keys, windows with mist bars and the [*] mark, glass header trays and the *@ glyph field (behind windows only). Do not introduce unrelated colors, shadows or type scales.
- The installed stylesheet imports `./_opencommerce-ds/brand.css` and `./_opencommerce-ds/theme.css` beside the main stylesheet. `brand.css` includes tokens and base styles. Keep both imports after `@import "tailwindcss"`. Let the installer configure fonts; do not add a second font loader.
- Put one control in each Field. Field connects labels, help, errors and required state. Validation and submission belong to your form. For Select use `value` and `onValueChange`, SelectTrigger with SelectValue, and SelectContent with SelectItem; values must be non-empty strings. Give the root a `name` for FormData. Use `defaultValue` only for uncontrolled input.
- Connect every action to its intended behavior. Handle empty, loading, disabled, invalid, success and error states. Preserve keyboard controls, focus return, accessible names and native form semantics. Never present a preview's local demo action as a completed backend operation.
- Use the provided portal behavior. Surface is for an isolated preview or a scoped theme; ordinary pages do not need an extra Surface wrapper. Mount one Toaster per application when using toast notifications.

## Render images

The CLI can render Open Graph images and social posts from copy you pass in. It does not open a browser. Colors, type and the logo come from the brand tokens and the bundled fonts and marks.

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds image templates --json
npx opencommerce-ds image --preset og --template lead --title "..." --text "..." --out og.png --json
npx opencommerce-ds image post --preset square --template announcement --title "..." --action "Get started" --json
npx opencommerce-ds image og --template frame --title "..." --image ./screen.png --format both --out ./images
npx opencommerce-ds image --template hero --preset og --chip "Product by Agentcard" --title "..." --text "..." --out og.png
npx opencommerce-ds image --template window --preset square --title "..." --image ./screen.png --label screen.png
npx opencommerce-ds image --template cards --preset portrait --title "..." --content cards.json
```

Presets are `og` (1200x630), `square` (1080x1080), `portrait` (1080x1350), `story` (1080x1920), `landscape` (1200x675, for X and LinkedIn), `x-banner` (1500x500) and `linkedin-banner` (1584x396), or any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` from 200 to 4000. `image` defaults to `og`. `image post` defaults to `square`. `image og` always renders 1200x630. Templates are `headline`, `lead` (a headline and a supporting line), `frame` (a screenshot in a window; pass `--image`, or `--text` for copy or code), `quote` (`--text` and optional `--by`) and `announcement` (a label, a headline and an optional key via `--action`). The brand image tool's four layouts are `hero` (chip, headline and line centered, a window rising from the bottom with code or your `--image`), `window` (words beside a window), `closing` (the mist card with the lockup and keys) and `cards` (numbered cards; `--cards` with blank lines between cards, heading first). They take `--chip`, `--action` and `--secondary` (the blue and white keys), `--label` (the window bar), `--code`, `--highlight`, `--seed`, `--no-logo`, `--no-glyphs` and `--no-window`, and open with the tool's own copy when you pass none. `--format` is `png` (the default), `svg` or `both`. `--ground` is `white` or `mist`. `--content file.json` reads the same fields, and flags override it.

`--json` prints the files written, with width, height and byte size. SVG text is outlined, so the file does not need the fonts installed. Headings and the wordmark use the bundled Helvetica-compatible display face, because Neue Haas Grotesk Display is not redistributable; body and keys use Inter; labels and code use the bundled monospace.

Pass `--preset all` to render every size. Give `--out` a directory when more than one file is written, or a `.png` or `.svg` path for a single file. A content file is a JSON object. Unknown fields, unknown templates, unknown presets and unknown grounds are errors. The same inputs write the same bytes.

## Read the brand system

These commands only report what is in the package. They do not invent a token, a font file or a logo.

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds manifest --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand system --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand tokens --group color --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand tokens --name=--ds-color-brand --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand fonts --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand logos --json
npx opencommerce-ds brand voice --json
npx opencommerce-ds principles --json
npx opencommerce-ds principles --surface product --json
```

`brand tokens --group` accepts `color`, `type`, `space`, `radius`, `motion` and `shadow`. `--name` must be the exact token, passed as `--name=--ds-color-brand` so the leading dashes are not read as a flag. `tokens <term>` still searches by substring, and a term that matches nothing is an error.

Fonts: Inter and JetBrains Mono are bundled, with their license files. The display face named in the tokens is not bundled. Renderers use the substitute face named by `brand fonts`. Do not download or invent a display font file.

Logos: `brand logos` returns the mark and the lockup, their files, and the do and do-not rules. There is no other logo file.

Voice: follow `brand voice`. The banned word list is closed. The product name stays lowercase.

Principles: `site` is the page system. `product` explains that this brand has no separate product theme. Build product UI with the site tokens and the registry. Do not invent a dark product palette.

## Use the component library

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds component list --json
npx opencommerce-ds component list --type ui --json
npx opencommerce-ds component inspect button --json
npx opencommerce-ds component emit button --state Site --json
npx opencommerce-ds component emit button --props '{"variant":"secondary","size":"sm"}' --text "Read the docs" --json
```

`component list` is the full catalog. `list` and `search` filter that catalog by words. `inspect` returns exports, parsed props, example state names, constraints and source. `emit --state` copies that example. `emit --props` checks every key and value against the parsed schema and errors on anything unknown. Pass `--text` for the child text. Do not pass `--state` and `--props` together. If a component has no parsed prop schema, emit a state instead of inventing JSX.

`show` and `view` remain the full registry record. Prefer `inspect` and `emit` when you need props and a snippet.

## Make slides, print files and illustrations

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds deck --list
npx opencommerce-ds deck --input deck.json --out deck          # a PNG per slide and deck.pdf
npx opencommerce-ds deck cover --title "..." --body "..."
npx opencommerce-ds merch --list
npx opencommerce-ds merch tee-front --out merch                # SVG at physical size and a 300 dpi PNG
npx opencommerce-ds merch sticker --guides                     # trim and safe lines for proofing
npx opencommerce-ds illustrate --list
npx opencommerce-ds illustrate field --size 1500x500 --seed 7
npx opencommerce-ds illustrate halftone --image ./photo.png
```

Slides are `cover`, `section`, `statement`, `bullets`, `stat`, `quote`, `image` and `end`, each a layout of the image tool at 1920x1080. `deck.json` holds `{ "slides": [ { "type": "cover", "title": "..." } ] }`; unknown slots error. Merch items are print files only (no mockups) with bleed and safe area; sizes are common vendor print areas, so confirm with the vendor. The brand has one ground, so merch prints on white or light blanks, and logos are the files in `brand/logo/` as drawn. Illustrations follow `brand/illustration.md`: glyphs on a lattice, faint ink, blue only where the site puts it.

## Work in Figma

The CLI never calls Figma. Each action writes files and prints the Figma MCP calls to make, in order.

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds figma tokens                               # variables JSON and use_figma scripts
npx opencommerce-ds figma push illustration field              # also asset, slide, component, page
npx opencommerce-ds figma pull "https://figma.com/design/<key>/x?node-id=1-2"
npx opencommerce-ds figma check figma/variables-1-2.json figma/design-1-2.txt
```

`figma check` lists every off-brand color, font, size, radius and space with the nearest token and exits 1 when there are any. Build from library components and tokens, never the raw Figma values.

## Render a short video

`video` renders a 2 second mp4 at 12 frames per second. It does not open a browser. Frames are SVG from the same tokens, bundled fonts and logo files as `image`, rasterized with system fonts off, then encoded with the pinned ffmpeg build and bitexact flags. The same inputs write the same bytes.

```sh
npx opencommerce-ds video templates --json
npx opencommerce-ds video --template social --size square --title "..." --text "..." --out clip.mp4 --json
npx opencommerce-ds video --template announcement --size vertical --title "..." --label "Now available" --action "Get started" --json
npx opencommerce-ds video --template product --size landscape --label order.ts --text "const order = { sku: \"cup\" }" --json
```

Templates are `social`, `announcement` and `product` (2 seconds at 12 fps), `hero`, `window`, `closing` and `cards` (the image tool's layouts, 4 seconds at 30 fps: they play in once on the ease-out token, staggered 60ms, and rest while the glyph field drifts as the site's does), `field` (6 seconds at 12 fps, the site's drift) and `mark` and `orbit` (6 seconds at 30 fps, the hero's swaying [*]). Sizes are `square` (1080x1080), `vertical` (1080x1920, 9:16) and `landscape` (1920x1080, 16:9). `--template` and `--size` are required. `--ground` is `white` or `mist`. `--out` is an `.mp4` or `.webm` file or a directory (default `.ds/videos`); `--format webm` also picks WebM. `--still <seconds>` writes one PNG frame instead. There is no other template, size, frame rate or duration.

## Verify before finishing

1. Run the consuming project's type checks, tests and production build.
2. Run `npx opencommerce-ds check --json`. Exit 0 means no token violations; exit 1 means unresolved violations or a command error. Read the JSON result, fix the findings and rerun. A token check does not test accessibility or behavior.
3. Test every interaction with mouse and keyboard. Submit invalid and valid forms, choose options, open and close overlays, and test loading/error paths. Check desktop and phone widths, focus visibility, overflow and reduced-motion behavior.
4. Compare screenshots against the relevant library previews and reference. `npx opencommerce-ds review http://localhost:3000 --any` can capture and review a running page. It requires playwright-core and Chromium. Automated scoring uses an available supported reviewer; if none is available, read the saved screenshots and report a manual review. Never claim an independent score that was not produced.
5. Report what changed, which checks passed, and any remaining limitations. If conversion left follow-up tasks, complete or report them explicitly.

## Instructions and hooks

`init` and conversion install AGENTS.md and a local `.ds/agent-guide.md`, plus supported agent instruction files and hook configuration. Agents that do not load those files automatically should read them explicitly. Hooks support Claude Code, Codex and Cursor when enabled by that tool; other agents run the CLI checks directly. Codex hook activation may require the user's `/hooks` trust step. No hook integration is required to use the components correctly.

Read-only commands: `guide`, `manifest`, `describe`, `brand`, `principles`, `component list`, `component inspect`, `component emit`, `list`, `show`, `look`, `tokens`, `check` without `--fix`, `image templates`, `video templates`, the `--list` of `deck`, `merch` and `illustrate`, `figma pull` and `figma check`.
Commands that write files: `init`, `add`, `apply`, the legacy bare conversion command, `check --fix`, `image` (image files), `video` (mp4, webm or png files), `deck`, `merch`, `illustrate` and `figma tokens|push` (files under `--out`), and review/snapshot state updates. Use `--dry-run` with `init`, `add` or conversion to inspect planned writes. JSON goes to stdout and progress goes to stderr. Unknown names and installation failures return a nonzero exit code. The error JSON is `{ "ok": false, "error": "..." }`.

## Project configuration and agent handoff

Start with `npx opencommerce-ds manifest --json`, then `info --json`, `search <term> --json` and `view <names...> --json`. These commands are read-only. `show` and `inspect` remain aliases of `view`. `component inspect` is the prop and state view.

`add` respects components.json, inherited TypeScript or JavaScript aliases, the target stylesheet and the package manager. It emits JSX/JS when `tsx` is false, installs the theme and agent guidance, and preserves differing local files. Use `add <names...> --diff` to review changes before `--overwrite`. Use `--cwd <app>` from a repository root. For shared workspace packages, use the upstream installer described below.

`create --template vite --name <directory>` scaffolds a new app and installs brand components. `init` configures an existing app; `init button card` also adds components. `apply --dry-run --json` previews a requested conversion of existing styles. Do not run conversion to discover or install the library.

Portable skills are installed in `.agents/skills/opencommerce-ds/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/opencommerce-ds/SKILL.md`; the full guide is `.ds/agent-guide.md`. Read `add --view` or the installed source for imports resolved to this project's paths. The installed brand utility is separate from the application's existing `lib/utils` exports.

The standard shadcn registry is configured under `@opencommerce-ds` in components.json. For workspace routing, install with `npx opencommerce-ds shadcn add @opencommerce-ds/theme @opencommerce-ds/button`. Include the theme explicitly with upstream shadcn so existing font and color aliases are updated. Native `add` applies it automatically.

Advanced operations use pinned shadcn 4.22.1: `shadcn <args...>`, `mcp`, `registry`, `preset`, `migrate`, `eject`, and `build`. These need network access on first use and preserve upstream output formats. Native brand commands accept `--json`. Preset/base changes are upstream operations that may change the brand; use them only when requested. MCP configuration alone does not prove the agent host has loaded its server.

The explicit `apply` command scopes color conversion to recognized components and preserves unrelated artwork and shared palette data. The legacy bare-command conversion remains for compatibility; use `apply` for new restyling tasks.
